conviction_note: Near-balanced: French peers BNP and SocGen beat this week, with SocGen's French retail NII up 13%, against a FICC slump at Barclays (-19% vs +2% expected) that hits FICC-heavy CACIB, and against negatives the company flagged itself on 5 Oct (P&C weather, Banco BPM PPA catch-up of about -EUR60m). The findings sum to +0.1, so the two measurements agree in sign and are both near zero.

findings.finding: French peers reported a strong Q3 this week: SocGen's net income beat by about 16% (Jefferies), with French retail NII +13% YoY, and BNP's EUR3.46bn net income beat FactSet's EUR3.28bn with revenue also ahead. This supports LCL's NII upturn, which CASA's own pre-close note says is in a 'strong upturn since Q4-25' with the high-single-digit 2026 guide maintained.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ACA fell on 6 of its last 9 results days, including the Q3-25 beat (-4.8%) and Q1-26 (-3.7%); it rose +2.6% on the Q2-26 beat (NIGS about EUR150m above consensus)
findings.original_quote: Strong upturn in NII since Q4-25 and high single digit guidance for 2026 maintained (CASA pre-close note, English original); peer: SocGen RNPG 'qui dépasse nettement les 1,62 milliard d'euros attendus par les analystes' (beating by a wide margin the EUR1.62bn analysts expected)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. ACA is +3.4% over 5 days alongside GLE and BNP, and +0.85% on 29 Oct while GLE rose +2.4% on its own beat. A full read-through would have taken ACA's 5-day move past the peers', and it has not. A 17-analyst name, so the residual is small.
findings.independence: BNP beat on the same day-type: https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/bnp-paribas-depasse-les-attentes-au-3e-trimestre-2026-avec-un-benefice-en-hausse_705027 ; the CASA pre-close note on LCL: https://www.credit-agricole.com/en/pdfPreview/211432

findings.finding: FICC had a weak Q3 at European peers. Barclays' FICC fell 19% YoY against a consensus of +2%, and SocGen's FICC was weaker per Jefferies. CACIB's capital-markets revenue is FICC-heavy with little equities to offset, and the pre-close note gives no quantified guide for it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CACIB was the driver of the Q3-24 and Q1-26 beats; no clean history of a CACIB miss isolated in the tape
findings.why_not_priced: Industry proxy, a week old; analysts had a week to mark CACIB FICC down after Barclays, so much of it should be in the bar. If fully priced, ACA would not have rallied with peers into the print. A GlobalCapital headline says BNP's Q3 was 'bolstered by FICC' but it is undated and paywalled, so the proxy is contested.

findings.finding: CASA's own Q3-26 pre-close note flags headwinds: P&C insurance hit by summer weather events in France and Italy (hail, droughts, wildfires; not quantified), a Banco BPM PPA catch-up of about -EUR60m in Q3, the loss of a EUR252m BPM revenue base in Q3-25, still-weak Leasys/mobility, and higher corporate tax rates in Italy, Poland and Ukraine.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4-25: NIGS 1.03bn against 1.1bn expected on the Banco BPM charge; the stock fell 3.0% on 4 Feb 2026
findings.original_quote: France and Italy were impacted by significant weather events during summer (hail, droughts, wild fires); In Q3-26, catch up of the first two quarters of 2026 to be considered, resulting in a total of c. -EUR60m to be recorded
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company published it for analysts to model, and RBC trimmed its estimates on the PPA catch-up. Only the unquantified weather hit to P&C and the additional PPA on the 19.8%-to-29.3% step-up remain open.
